title: Quality Power Electrical Equipments Ltd - 544367 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR 1,000 crore (INR 1,007 cr, +157% YoY) with 23.5% EBITDA margin, despite a INR 25.7 crore non-cash Ind AS 29 charge.
summary.overview: Management reported first-ever INR 1,000 crore+ annual consolidated revenue, FY26 EBITDA of INR 236 crore (up 98%) and PAT of INR 185 crore (up 85%), above the revised guidance of about INR 900 crore revenue and 22% margin. Q4 was the highest-ever quarter at about INR 310 crore total revenue, but consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 19.1% from 27.9% in Q3 because of a INR 25.7 crore Ind AS 29 net monetary loss at Turkish subsidiary Endoks and one-time Labour Code provisions. Order book exiting FY26 was above INR 1,400 crore. FY27 guidance is muted at about 15-20% growth as new capacity ramps, with management expecting above 50% growth in FY28.

segments.name: Quality Power (standalone, incl. projects)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR 246 crore per management; EBIT margin about 33% for Quality Power and 21% for QP projects. Order book above INR 520 crore, with data-centre order book about INR 520 crore cited in Q&A.

segments.name: Mehru Electrical and Mechanical Engineers
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR 318 crore; margin about 20% in Q4 and 15% for the year; annualised EBIT margin about 15%. Order book about INR 430 crore; management sees only 30-35% further capacity headroom at current plant.

segments.name: Endoks Energy (Turkey)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR 468 crore; reported EBIT margin 23% including Ind AS 29 effect, about 29-30% without it; management cites about 32% EBITDA on stable-currency basis. Order book about INR 450 crore; Q4 cash flow about INR 136 crore.

segments.name: Sukrut (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Turnaround underway; losses halved versus last year and management targets 70-75% growth this year without losses.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: about 15-20% growth in revenue and margin band of 15-20%, reflecting an S-curve stabilisation year; growth to resume above 50% in FY28 (management said this is 'correct' when asked).
Order book target of INR 1,500-1,800 crore before start of FY27 per management.
Expect some near-term gross margin pressure in Q1-Q2 FY27 from raw material and commodity price increases; pass-through to customers is with a lag.

Targeted BESS converter orders of USD 60-80 million this year against USD 31 million current BESS order book; PCS factory in Turkey (about USD 2 million investment) expected to start billing by Q4 FY26 or Q1 FY27.
Dividend: final dividend of INR 1 per share recommended; promoters waived their entitlement.
capex_capacity: New Sangli factory (global coil, HVDC, PCS, CTC, magnet wire) expected to commence operations around July-August 2026; management also said trial production by end-2026 and project managers stick to Dec-Jan start; commissioning on track for Q3 FY27 per CFO.
New high-voltage test laboratory to be commissioned alongside the new factory.

Mehru: additional oven capacity post-September 2026; GIS manufacturing and testing infrastructure with first prototypes around July-August 2026; INR 17.2 crore capex for GIS and HV testing equipment. Current plant saturation at about 30-35% above FY26 output of about INR 320 crore.
Endoks: new PCS facility at Nigde targeted for December 2026; new BESS manufacturing facility on in-house technology; 1,725 kW PCS inverter expected to launch within next two quarters.
Capital WIP of INR 73 crore; management says Sangli peak revenue potential of about INR 1,500 crore subject to CTC cable expansion and insulator supply.
demand_pricing: Order book exiting FY26 above INR 1,400 crore (about 1.4x FY26 revenue); Q4 order intake about INR 870 crore per corrected figure, with INR 300 crore executed in the quarter.
Pipeline of opportunities above INR 1,100 crore for QP alone across FACTS, renewables and data centres; demand cited across Middle East, Europe, US and Australia.
BESS: management sees BESS PCS as 40-50% of project cost; converter margins about 10-12% at bid level, targeted to reach 17-18% at volume; battery pass-through about 2-3%.

Data centres: first US data-centre order of about INR 49 crore won; management expects a couple more projects in coming quarters; US reactor market for data centres sized at about INR 1,500 crore per year by management.

Supply chain constraints: insulator deliveries running 18-24 months; cable constraints mitigated by vertical integration. Order intake in Sangli and Delhi largely closed for next quarter; only strategic orders being taken.
Transformer bids in US (USD 80-100 million) were largely lost; management is not prioritising transformers at lower margins.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the BESS and data-centre opportunity and what products will be supplied?
qa_highlights.answer: BESS order book about USD 31 million with a further USD 30-50 million expected by year-end; management targets USD 60-80 million of orders this year and sees a billion-dollar opportunity. Data-centre orders are booked out with 6-7 month delivery timelines.

qa_highlights.question: Who are the BESS competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Chinese players are seen as the largest competition; GE is at a high price level and not yet competed with directly. Company says it competes on software/EMS and service in Europe, US and Australia.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance for FY27 revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance of about 15-20% growth in FY27; traditional HV margins are steady with a couple of points of pressure from conflict-related price increases; BESS converter margins are in an investment phase.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 revenue flat QoQ and what is the Endoks seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Mehru's Q4 is its highest-profit quarter and Endoks' Q1 is seasonally muted; it reports Endoks on a Jan-Dec basis so QoQ comparison is not like-for-like.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fundraising plan given about INR 250 crore cash?
qa_highlights.answer: The USD 75 million enabling resolution is a dry-powder authorisation, not an immediate raise; company says it will draw much lower than the cap, cash is needed for organic growth and acquisitions, and it prefers zero debt.

qa_highlights.question: What is the other expenses increase in Q4 beyond the Ind AS 29 charge?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said freight outward of about INR 12 crore and liquidated damages of about INR 5 crore (pre-acquisition Mehru item, since curtailed) also rose other expenses; net monetary loss was INR 25 crore.

risks_watch: Ind AS 29 treatment at Endoks creates quarter-to-quarter swings in other expenses and reported margins (Q3 net monetary gain vs Q4 loss of INR 25.7 crore); management states it is non-cash and symmetric, but reported margins will fluctuate with index movements.
Supply chain: insulator lead times of 18-24 months and winding conductor shortages are delaying projects; management said the board is considering an insulator solution without details.
Raw material and commodity price inflation with a lag in pass-through; management flagged possible Q1-Q2 FY27 margin dip, with no price-variation clauses noted by analysts.
Commissioning timelines slipping: Sangli plant guided to July-August 2026 with trial production by end-2026; Endoks Nigde PCS facility targeted December 2026.
Turkey geopolitical exposure: management says operations are stable after 16 years, but analysts flagged India-Turkey tensions; Turkey also hosts BESS PCS ramp.

Governance and dilution: promoters and management waived incremental salary (second year) and dividend entitlement tied to the fundraise; enabling resolution for USD 75 million; BDNA committee evaluating acquisitions larger than cash on hand.
Disclosure inconsistencies to verify: order inflow quoted as INR 600 crore then corrected to INR 870 crore; Mehru and Endoks EBIT and EBITDA margin figures were given on differing bases.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and long-term BESS, GIS and HVDC opportunities, but explicitly cautious on FY27: muted 15-20% growth guidance, supply-chain constraints and near-term margin pressure. Management was defensive on the Ind AS 29 charge, repeatedly characterising it as optics, and somewhat evasive on fundraising use, insulator capacity and order-book breakdowns by entity.

key_quotes: This, in all honesty, is the Duckworth-Lewis of our financial year.
The good news is that this is a non-cash adjustment. The operating performance of the business and the cash it has generated are unaffected.
So, in Sangli and Delhi, we have almost closed our order intake for the next quarter.
The funds will be called as and when required and not necessarily immediately.
I would strongly encourage analysts to model Endoks on an Ind AS 29 normalized basis when projecting forward, treating these monetary loss or gain entries as below-the-line non-operating items.
We are currently facing certain execution challenges related to insulators and winding conductors.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at about 15-20% (midpoint 17.5%) as new Sangli factory ramps from roughly July-August 2026, backed by a FY26-exit order book above INR 1,400 crore and a targeted INR 1,500-1,800 crore order book, though the brief gives no explicit revenue-to-capacity bridge and FY27 is framed as a stabilisation year with near-term gross margin pressure.
